_why_overrides_workbench_base: Fix round 1 (Task 4 review). The first version of this file shipped
`overrides: []`, reasoned from the wrong scope: every rule below is
`subtree`, and `no_two_components_claim_one_destination_without_declaring_it`
only polices `file` rules, so nothing here was ever a *rule-level*
collision needing a declaration. But `overrides` is not read by that test
alone — a later stage reads it at the *file* level, to tell a BoingBag
deliberately replacing a file from `declared_by_the_owner_component` from
a genuine surprise. Measured directly against the owner's real media
(Task 4 review): every one of BoingBag 3.9-1's 210 files sits at a path
the base AmigaOS 3.9 recipe's `workbench-base` component already writes —
100%, not merely 'some'. Leaving `overrides` empty made that whole
measured fact invisible to whatever reads it, which is worse than not
declaring anything: a constant `declared: false` on every one of a
BoingBag's rows tells a reader nothing, which is exactly the noise this
field exists to separate a real surprise from (spec §3).
`recipe.rs`'s `every_override_names_a_component_that_exists` originally
could not resolve this anyway: it checked `recipe.component(over)` against
the one-component pseudo-`Recipe` `shipped_recipes()` built for a package,
which never contains `workbench-base` — a different recipe's component
entirely. Fixed there (Task 4 review) by resolving `over` against the
union of every shipped id, releases and packages together, rather than
one recipe's own list — see `all_shipped_component_ids` in `recipe.rs`.
name: BoingBag 3.9-1
_why_releases: ART-209. A BoingBag is an AmigaOS 3.9 archive and there is no such thing
as a BoingBag for 3.2 — 3.2's own updates arrive as a release component
(`Update3.2.1` in amigaos-3.2.json), not as a package. Until this field
existed nothing could say so, and the owner choosing AmigaOS 3.2 was
offered BoingBags on the screen below the component checklist.
3.9 only, and not '3.9 and anything later': ART ships two recipes and a
third would be a new JSON file, at which point whether these apply to it
is a question somebody has to answer by looking, not a default.
_why_no_distinguished_by: ART-167 gave a package a second identity fact for archives whose
top-level directory is shared. This one's is not: across all 44 `.lha`
archives in the owner's package folder, exactly one carries
`LocaleUpdate` is claimed by eight and `BoingBag3.9-2` by two.
So no `distinguished_by` is declared, deliberately. A condition that
separates nothing cannot help, and it can hurt: a user whose own copy
is a repack without the exact inner path named here would be told the
archive is missing when it is not. Spec §89's rule about not
claiming more than is true cuts this way too.
_why_host_placement_block: ART-166, measured in Task 8's real run and confirmed three independent
ways (ART's own reader, 7-Zip 26.02, the raw general-purpose flag word
0x0003 with bit 0 set): the `AmigaOS-Update` member named above is a
ZIP whose every entry is ZipCrypto-encrypted — 233 of 233 entries in
3.9-1's payload, 147 of 147 in 3.9-2's. The password belongs to the
BoingBag's own `Updater`, which the wrapper LHA carries beside the
payload and which has to run *on* an Amiga; every established
distribution builder (HstWB Installer, AmiKit, AmigaSYS, ClassicWB)
installs a BoingBag by running that Updater inside an emulator rather
than by decrypting anything, and the owner's recorded decision is that
So the rules below are right and unreachable, and spec §10/§89 says ART
must not offer what it cannot do. Declaring the block here — data, not
code — is what makes the screen refuse the tick with a translated
sentence naming the Updater, instead of accepting it and meeting the
reader's own raw English `Password required to decrypt file` after the
user already confirmed. The day the Amiga-side install round lands,
this one key is deleted and nothing else changes.
_why_amiga_installer: Measured, not assumed (2026-08-20, 7-Zip 26.02 against the owner's own
BoingBag39-1.lha). Two readings:
1. `BoingBag3.9-1\C\Updater` is a real entry, 25 588 bytes — so
relative to the archive's top-level directory the path is
`C/Updater`. The AmigaOS 3.9 release recipe shipped fourteen paths
nobody had read out of the medium and every one was wrong; that is
why this was read rather than guessed, even though the guess would
have been right this time.
2. The package's own `Install` script, line 858, runs it as
`(run (cat "C/Updater AmigaOS-Update \"" #target "\""))` — so the
first argument is the payload member and the second is the target
volume. Only the first is written here: the second is not a fact
about the package at all but about the run, and it is
`PlannedRun.system_volume`, supplied by whoever composes the run.
A recipe naming a volume is refused outright (`validate_installer`)
precisely so that decision cannot migrate into this file.
`AmigaOS-Update` is written here as well as in `member` above, and the
two are different facts for the same reason `member` and
`distinguished_by` are in the 3.9-2 recipe: `member` says where ART
would read this package's payload from the host, this says what the
package's own Updater is handed. They coincide today.
What is deliberately NOT declared: `Install`, the Installer script that
wraps this. It asks questions — the CD-ROM prompt at line 843, the
language and target requesters — and an unattended run would sit on the
first one until the deadline. The Updater is the step that needs the
Amiga, because it is the step holding the password (ART-166).
_why_minimum_version_and_overlay: ART-186, measured 2026-08-21 with 7-Zip 26.02 against the owner's own
downloads in E:\amiga\Amigatolon\os39, and then by reading each
extracted file's own $VER: marker rather than its length:
BoingBag39-1.lha      BoingBag3.9-1\C\Updater
BoingBag39-1-UAE.lha  BoingBag3.9-1-UAE\BoingBag3.9-1\C\Updater
BoingBag39-2.lha      BoingBag3.9-2\C\Updater
The UAE archive's own Readme names the build and what it fixes:
"This archive contains a file, Updater 45.15, that fixes the following
problem: You can install the BoingBag on UAE now. Tested with
AmigaForever 4.0 from Cloanto." It also says a download made after
2001-04-20 already carries the fix; the owner's is dated 2001-04-03, so
it does not — and this round runs that program inside an emulator.
So 45.15 is written here and 25 588 is not. A size is not an identity —
it is consistent with any build that happens to be that long — and
reading a coincidence as proof is the mistake that shipped an AmigaOS
3.5 tree under the name 3.9. The $VER: string is the file's own
statement about itself.
The overlay's `from` is a whole path from the UAE archive's own root,
including its top-level drawer, because that archive is one drawer
deeper than the package it patches: its Updater is at
BoingBag3.9-1-UAE\BoingBag3.9-1\C\Updater, not BoingBag3.9-1\C\Updater.
Extracting it over the package with an overwrite policy would have
written a parallel BoingBag3.9-1-UAE drawer and left 45.13 exactly where
it was. That was read out of the archive rather than reasoned about.
`to` is empty: the readme's own remedy is "copying the contents within
the BoingBag3.9-1 drawer in this package to it", so those contents land
on the package's own drawer.
BoingBag 3.9-2 declares no minimum_version, deliberately. Its own
Updater is 45.19 and no source says any build of it is unfit for an
emulator; declaring 45.19 there would be ART inventing a requirement
nobody stated, which is the same §89 mistake from the other side.
_why_required_medium: ART-193, and it was read out of the program rather than reasoned about.
The Updater this recipe launches verifies the original AmigaOS 3.9
CD-ROM before it does anything. Its own printable strings, read on the
host on 2026-08-21 from the owner's own `BoingBag39-1 (1).lha`:
Checking AmigaOS 3.9 CD-ROM ...
Failed to check AmigaOS 3.9 CD-ROM.
Did you really insert a original AmigaOS 3.9 CD-ROM
into a mounted CD-ROM drive?
AmigaOS3.9:Videos/Angels.avi
AmigaOS3.9:Audio/Circle Orbital.mp3
AmigaOS3.9:OS-Version3.9/Workbench3.9/WBStartup/AmiDock
Without that volume the program opens its own screen and never
finishes — measured three times against the owner's real tree, up to
1 200 s, with not one of the 3 795 files written.
`AmigaOS3.9` is written here without a colon because it is a volume
name, and because that is the name the disc itself states: the owner's
AmigaOS39.iso carries the ISO 9660 volume identifier `AmigaOS3.9`, read
by ART's own `core::iso` reader and confirmed with 7-Zip. The command
layer asks the image what it is called and refuses a mismatch, so this
line is a claim ART checks rather than one it trusts.
Note for whoever reads the two BoingBags side by side: 45.15 looks for
`Circle Orbital.mp3` and 45.19 for `Circle - Orbital.mp3`, and the disc
carries the latter. That difference is the Updater's, not ART's, and it
is recorded because it is exactly the kind of thing that makes one
build behave differently from another on the same disc.
